scope: The 80 environments added in PR #50 relative to the original 75. Four core capabilities at each canonical baseline, with source-reviewed exceptions for the five difficulties and two interaction modes. The resulting 800 profile labels are not 800 independent audits.
method: Read each environment's generator, visible browser implementation, grader, verifier, solver and control profiles; classify normal screenshot-only solutions. Primary review adjudicated competing interpretations into binary capability labels. Source-review limitations are evidence notes, not a third label. No new gameplay, human calibration, real-time classification or difficulty assignment is claimed.
temporal_scope: Configuration-aware source classification; the dedicated temporal audit and empirical calibration remain separate. Live and paused clock modes share the same capability label under the settled definition.
historical_preservation: The original 75 legacy temporal annotations and frozen temporal pilot are unchanged. Original first-pass reviews and the pre-adjudication report were preserved separately; each entry records its first-pass SHA-256.

baseline_description.interaction: Turn through edge arrows and drag tray objects directly onto scene geometry or onto another tray object.
baseline_description.difficulty: The source-selected baseline: six unmarked fixed views, three wards, a four-digit dial, a five-colour sequence, and two separate inventory combinations.

rationale.visual: The solution requires locating objects and destinations in fixed 2D pictures, matching inventory glyphs and object names to depicted affordances, reading a number, and discriminating the spatial order of coloured beads. CSS perspective gives some objects depth styling, but the action contract uses view identifiers and 2D rectangles; no depth reconstruction, 3D rotation, or perspective alignment is required. This remains true at every listed difficulty and in both interaction modes.
rationale.temporal: The number and colour evidence is visible only in the desk and gallery views respectively; the controls for entering it exist in the door view. Navigation replaces the scene and closes the lock overlay. Although revealed clues persist when revisited and partially entered codes remain stored, a screenshot-only agent must retain at least some clue information across the intervening view change. The label therefore follows hidden earlier-state memory, not a simple visible sequence or the decorative door animation. D1 retains the separate three-digit clue and door; D2 adds the separate colour clue; D4 and D5 additionally require retaining the reading directions discovered in another view. Both input surfaces preserve this memory demand.
rationale.reasoning_planning: Successful actions have explicit dependencies: discover both components, join frame plus lens, apply the loupe to reveal the numbered ward evidence; separately join handle plus wire, retrieve a key with the hook, and use that key at the door. The visible instructions describe joining and using objects without supplying these recipes or destinations, so the agent must infer useful combinations and applications. Three wrong entries seize a ward, making unsupported lock guesses consequential. D1 and D2 still require the loupe dependency chain; D4 and D5 add a separately discovered rule for whether to reverse each clue. Reducing views, adding decoys, changing code lengths, or replacing dragging with selection does not remove the supported reasoning label.
rationale.exploration_interface: The initial screen does not expose the necessary clues, components, or recipes. The agent must choose room objects to inspect, expose concealed contents, and test or infer inventory combinations and uses. In the baseline these scene hotspots have no semantic text labels or tab-order discovery aid, and the artwork alone does not disclose which objects react. This is active information gathering across a room, beyond routine feedback after an instructed step. D1 and D2 add visual wear cues but still conceal the frame and lens and require discovering how their combination reveals the clue. Simplified interaction explains its selection controls but does not reveal those task facts; D4 and D5 require an additional drawer inspection for the order card. No profile supplies a complete visible solution at the start.

source_evidence.claim: Scene targets are generated as jittered normalized 2D rectangles with a fixed view identifier; no depth coordinate participates in the affordance geometry.
The browser places named inventory cards and pictured scene hotspots using the generated 2D geometry.
Drawer, radiator, and grate perspective transforms are fixed artwork styling; clues are presented as legible digits, a row of coloured beads, and, at higher difficulties, arrows.
Full-mode manipulation is checked by source and destination rectangles plus drag travel; it does not require geometric reasoning in three dimensions.
Digits render only in deskScene after loupe use, coloured beads render only in galleryScene after sheet removal, and the ward-entry dialogs display the agent's entries without displaying those clues.
Rendering replaces the room with only the currently selected scene. Navigation closes the lock and renders the new view; the persistent tray, counters, and readout do not copy the clue values.

A ward can be submitted only from view zero after its clue was uncovered, and the guess must equal the generated clue-derived answer. This establishes the clue-to-door information dependency independently of the private-state solver.
Availability flags implement concealed components and tool-use dependencies; the recipes are frame plus lens to loupe and, for D3-D5, handle plus wire to hook.

The browser consumes valid component pairs into tools, rejects invalid pairs, and requires the corresponding tool for clue revelation, key retrieval, and key-ward release. These are actual action consequences.
Replay enforces availability, inventory, recipes, correct tool applications, prior clue revelation, and release of all wards before the exit can open.

Pictured hotspots are conditionally rendered, generically labelled as room objects, and excluded from sequential focus. Flipping the label, opening the drawer or floor tile, removing the sheet, and opening the order drawer expose previously unavailable objects or clues.
The visible interface gives general use-or-join instructions and navigation controls, but does not print the tool recipes, hidden clue values, or a prescribed sequence of inspection targets.
Clear and subtle cue profiles add a drop shadow to pictured affordances; they do not disclose hidden contents or tool-use rules.

The shared developer answer panel is absent unless the separate cheat mode is enabled; it is not a normal persistent clue display in the canonical UI. The associated URL gate at lines 127-129 and installer at lines 1284-1338 were also inspected.

Baseline is D3/full. All five difficulty profiles retain the frame-and-lens chain; D1 has a number ward, D2 adds colour, D3 adds the key chain, D4 adds clue directions, and D5 adds longer clues and two decoys. The paired input surfaces are drag/use and select/click.
Higher-profile reading directions determine whether the number and colour clues are reversed, adding cross-view information without changing the provisional temporal label.
Both modes bind the same scene operations, ward controls, and inventory effects. Simplified mode substitutes selected-item clicks for inventory dragging, without exposing hidden clues or recipes.
The exported verifier independently loads the environment grader and replays the exported result against truth and public state rather than accepting the browser pass label.

The scripted solver reads state and takes ward answers from runtime_lock_answers; its success strategy is private-state wiring evidence, not evidence that a screenshot-only agent can avoid remembering the visible clues.

after_hours_at_the_reliquary.review_scope: Read the complete first-pass decisions, visible solution, rationales, and source-evidence claims; spot-checked generator, browser, grader, and solver passages. This is not an independent complete-source second annotation or gameplay test.

baseline_description.interaction: Click or marquee ants on the map, press G/S/D/M, click a visible destination, use R at the brood chamber, and pan with edge controls or the minimap.
baseline_description.difficulty: The original uncontrolled configuration: five workers balance a 40-tick scout, an exact two-worker/70-work excavation, seed trips, production, one moving four-raider interception, and a later assault.

rationale.visual: The necessary geometry consists of ant positions, selectable groups, destination markers, two planar tunnel branches, a scrolling horizontal viewport, and its minimap. The enemy formation's vertical displacement must be understood relative to NORTH and SOUTH. All task positions and hit tests are x/y geometry; underground theming adds no required depth reasoning.
rationale.temporal: The formation oscillates vertically after the interception band opens. The accepted branch is the sign of its vertical velocity at the command tick, not its current vertical position. A single position can correspond to either direction, and neither the HUD nor ant orientation supplies a static velocity indicator. The agent must interpret recent movement and issue its one commitment within the active band while that direction still applies. The branch choice is enforced by both browser simulation and replay grader, and passing requires every wave to be intercepted. The automatic gathering, scouting-completion, production, and assault animations are not needed as independent temporal evidence. All five difficulty profiles retain this motion-dependent interception in both interaction modes.
rationale.reasoning_planning: Worker assignments determine whether the brood becomes available and how seeds accumulate; soldier production consumes those seeds. The agent must prepare enough defenders before committing, because insufficient defenders cause a breach, correct interceptions kill some defenders, and the later assault requires enough surviving or newly produced soldiers to remove the rival queen's HP. The visible instructions specify the opening worker roles, but the agent still chooses production and force allocation with consequences for defense and the later assault. D1 removes digging and scouting but retains resource-to-soldier preparation, interception losses, and the later assault. D4 adds sequential reuse after losses; D5 adds disjoint commitments during overlapping waves. These change the decisions without changing the capability label.
rationale.exploration_interface: At D3, the enemy queen, rival outposts, formation motion, and contact panel are hidden until the player actively assigns a worker to the listening front and leaves that assignment in place. This information-acquisition action is necessary: simply letting time advance does not reveal the rival, and defense commands are rejected while contact is absent. The positive label rests on revealing the concealed opponent through scouting, not on learning the displayed hotkeys, ordinary command feedback, or panning to a known destination. The reveal persists, so it does not require later recall of a vanished scout report. D2, D4, and D5 preserve this requirement; D1 starts with contact available and has no scouting requirement. Simplified mode changes selection and command entry but retains the same concealment and reveal logic.

configuration_exceptions.reason: D1 sets hidden_opening to false and scout_ticks to zero, and starts with the brood ready. Contact and rival queen information are available from the start; outposts and formations appear automatically as their scheduled world events occur. The later CONTACT IN BAND status is ordinary progression, and the disclosed map/minimap plus explicit controls suffice. In full mode the agent may pan to click the rival marker, but its position and HP are already available on the minimap/HUD; no scout reveal or interface experiment is necessary.

source_evidence.claim: D1 explicitly uses brood_ready=true, dig_workers=0, hidden_opening=false, and scout_ticks=0.

Without hidden_opening, contact starts acquired, the rival queen is drawn and its HP displayed, the minimap exposes its position, and outposts/raids appear through automatic world progression. Scout and excavation controls are omitted for the D1 parameters.

The map projects x/y positions directly into a planar viewport, draws labeled north/south tunnels and destination markers, exposes a minimap, and uses matching 2D radii and tunnel strips for selection and targeting. Ant rendering does not encode the changing formation heading.

After the band opens, formation y follows a sine wave while the correct branch follows the corresponding cosine sign. Commitments are accepted only in the response interval and only once per unresolved wave. The UI draws formation positions and a band-status panel without showing the correct branch as static text.

Replay independently computes the movement-based branch at the command tick, rejects commands outside the active band, and requires every wave to have been successfully intercepted. Merely surviving a wrongly intercepted wave cannot pass.

Exact digging crews unlock production, gather orders generate spendable seeds, raising soldiers consumes seeds, and interception casualties reduce the force available for the later one-damage-per-soldier assault. Persistent HUD values support replenishing the force after observing losses.

The grader enforces defense group size, casualties, the prerequisite that raids resolve before assault, and exclusion of soldiers already reserved for an unresolved interception. D5 therefore needs separate groups while both commitments remain active.

Hidden-opening configurations start without contact. Only completion of an active scout assignment reveals the opponent; reassigning that scout cancels the acquisition. Enemy queen, outposts, formations, minimap enemy information, and the contact panel are concealed before that reveal, and interception commands require contact.
Replay preserves the same initial concealment and scout-completion transition and rejects defense orders issued before contact, making the information-acquisition prerequisite part of accepted play.

The canonical baseline is difficulty 3/full. D1 starts with brood and contact ready; D2 uses one digger; D3-D5 use two diggers; D4 has sequential raids and D5 overlapping raids. Both interaction profiles are implemented. None removes the resource, interception, and assault dependency.

Every difficulty profile generates raid windows and a hidden seeded phase offset, and retains the same tick-based formation/interception mechanism. World parameters change raid counts, timings, and prerequisites rather than replacing motion interpretation with a visible lane answer.

Full mode selects ants through map clicks or marquee and uses displayed hotkeys plus destinations; simplified mode provides roster selection and explicit command buttons. Both call the same simulation actions. Hotkeys and command-panel operation themselves provide no separate evidence of exploratory learning.

The solver compares screenshots to obtain the movement direction, but also reads public_state.json, exact layout coordinates, counts, and schedule details. Its private implementation access is not treated as a permissible screenshot-only solution or as gameplay verification.
The exported verifier loads the exported transcript and invokes the independent Anthill Front grader, so the replayed dependencies and victory requirements also govern exported verification.

baseline_description.interaction: Jar drag and duration-based pestle control.
baseline_description.difficulty: The exact original configuration: six jars, four dependent route commits, nine grind notches, four bone spurs, one vortex, four effect seals, and the original recovery budgets and tolerances.

rationale.visual: The necessary geometry is planar: compare a curved preview with a guide's center and tangent direction, locate the flask and effect discs, and use the cabinet/mortar controls. Paths, distances, headings, bone polygons, and vortex discs all operate in two map coordinates. The visual styling does not create a depth-dependent decision.
rationale.temporal: Full grinding requires sustaining and releasing the pestle: the grind notch increases once per 240 ms of a hold and changes the candidate path. Routes use varied, distinct grind outcomes, so a general Full solution cannot use only the initial unground setting. This is duration control even if the agent uses measured holds and inspects static previews after release. Fog is cumulative, the current guide and active preview remain visible, and stirring advances in discrete clicks; these features do not independently establish a temporal-memory requirement. The temporal label is provisional for this baseline audit.
rationale.reasoning_planning: The agent must infer and satisfy the guide's joint center-and-heading constraint through the relationship between jar choice, grind, and resulting path. Committing a path fixes its geometry, consumes stock on completion, and changes the origin from which the next choice is made; a misaligned path changes position without advancing the route. Success requires all route guides to be passed before sealing the requested disc. This is a concrete causal constraint and sequence of dependent choices, although the always-visible next guide permits local decisions without planning the entire hidden route or deliberately exercising recovery.
rationale.exploration_interface: Jar labels show names and glyphs, not their randomly generated direction, length, curvature, or turn. A path becomes visible only after a jar is loaded, and its grind response must be revealed by operating the pestle or notch controls. The agent can safely probe and replace candidate ingredients before committing. The UI presents the goal and tool labels but no tutorial explaining the route or tool behavior. This required discovery of action effects supports exploration; merely receiving the next guide or exposing fog along a correct committed path would not suffice by itself. The private-state solver's supplied solution and recovery probe are not information available to screenshot-only play.

configuration_exceptions.reason: Across every difficulty, Simplified selects jars by click and sets curvature with a stationary notch button. Each candidate can be judged against the persistent current guide from a static screenshot; no earlier candidate must be remembered because it can be selected again. Stirring and recovery are discrete actions, the revealed map accumulates rather than disappearing, and the next guide is directly displayed after route completion. A general solution can repeatedly inspect static candidate paths and commit a match without interpreting motion, sustaining an evolving input, or recalling hidden earlier route state. This exception is provisional with the rest of the temporal audit. All five difficulty profiles retain the same planar path/guide constraints and the need to reveal jar behavior, so no other capability exception is supported.

source_evidence.claim: The five profiles change inventory size, dependent route count, notch resolution, field geometry, and budgets; none changes the basic path, preview, or cumulative-reveal mechanics.
Simplified jar loading is a stationary click.
Simplified renders clickable notch buttons and sets the selected notch immediately, with no hold or elapsed-time calculation.

All revealed positions continue clearing fog; the accumulated trail, active remaining path, current guide, and flask remain drawn. The trace need not be interpreted as motion to choose the next ingredient.
Stir, water, and bellows each compute a completed state transition synchronously per click, so these actions require no duration control or moving-target interception.
The grader accepts direct notch selection specifically for Simplified, confirming that this untimed control is a legitimate interface-specific solution.
Candidate paths use x/y coordinates and constant curvature; guide matching checks both center distance and path heading.
The visible route guide draws a center bead and oriented guide lines/arcs in the map plane.
Full pestle input starts an ongoing hold, advances grind from elapsed time, and requires release to stop the evolving notch state.

Generated route schedules sample distinct notch values and require every guide to uniquely identify its ingredient-and-notch choice at the route's current position. This prevents treating the canonical route as a fixed sequence of unground actions.
Replay binds grind start/tick/release to Full and direct grind setting to Simplified. The browser's duration behavior, rather than a metadata capability tag, establishes the Full temporal demand.

The first stir freezes the candidate path and its guide alignment. Subsequent clicks move along that path; completion spends an ingredient and advances the route only when the path was aligned and was not interrupted by a vortex.

Final success requires the requested effect, every route guide completed, and compliance with ingredient, water, bellows, and hazard limits. Merely reaching a visually matching effect is insufficient.

The contract verifies that each guide uniquely identifies its visible path, every generated correct segment is unobstructed, and the composed route ends at the target. Correct local guide choices supply a general route without mandatory hazard probing or recovery.
Ingredient identity/order, direction, path length, curvature, and turn vary during generation; jar names do not specify these action effects.

Only the active ingredient supplies a path preview. The current route guide is drawn separately after the fog layer, so discovering the candidate ingredient's behavior requires interaction while the comparison target remains available.
Loading or replacing an uncommitted ingredient resets its grind and displays its path without incrementing ingredient spend, permitting safe causal probing.

The visible cabinet contains jar names/glyphs; the rest of the UI shows the ordered sigil, mortar, grind track, tool labels, stock, and seal control. It does not display ingredient vectors or an explanatory route tutorial.

The implementation solver reads ground_truth.json and follows its solution list after an explicitly supplied recovery exercise. Its known route and private-state waits cannot be used as evidence that screenshot-only agents already know the choices or must exercise recovery.
The exported verifier loads result, ground truth, and public state and delegates to the same independent replay grader, preserving the route and final-effect success constraints.

apothecary_dead_reckoning.review_scope: Read the complete first-pass decisions, visible solution, rationales, and source-evidence claims; checked browser passages implementing previews, loading, duration-based grinding, route commits, and simplified notch controls. This is not an independent complete-source second annotation or gameplay test.

baseline_description.interaction: Hold Space to drive the winch upward and release Space to let the same momentum-bearing cage fall.
baseline_description.difficulty: The baseline combines a narrow inertial cage, all four drift laws, a short motion wake, and a distant late crate whose service competes with a rapidly draining specimen meter.

rationale.visual: Success depends on comparing the cage's vertical interval with the full visible height of the specimen and crate, including distance to the shaft boundaries. Every object lies on the same screen-plane vertical track; no depth, viewpoint transformation, or 3D relationship is required. All five difficulty profiles and both interaction modes preserve this geometry.
rationale.temporal: Space must remain held or released for appropriate durations while cage velocity accumulates and the specimen moves, reverses, or changes speed. A current position alone does not establish cage momentum; specimen wake samples encode recent motion. Capture also integrates time inside and outside the cage, and the UI does not retain visible progress totals. In simplified mode HAUL and COAST latch the same evolving acceleration, so the player still must control when to switch them. The trend beacon and longer wake at difficulties 1 and 2 reduce motion estimation demands but do not remove sustained control or overlap-duration requirements. This is an action-timing demand, not observation-only temporal understanding.
rationale.reasoning_planning: One cage serves two targets with competing consequences: time away from the specimen drains its reserve, crate containment accumulates persistent salvage progress, and completing specimen capture before crate completion is a terminal failure. The player must choose when to track the specimen, visit the crate, return for reserve, and finally finish capture, while anticipating braking distance. These dependencies are implemented in the simulation and replay grader, rather than inferred merely from motion or private-state solver complexity. Every difficulty keeps these two-target meter rules; wider cages and more forgiving rates do not remove the ordering and allocation decisions. Generator filtering supplies supporting evidence against the reference specimen-only policy, not a proof that all alternative specimen-only policies fail.
rationale.exploration_interface: The task states the goal and HAUL/COAST control semantics, and the specimen, crate and cage overlap are visible. Hidden fill meters reduce feedback quality, but the player can service the crate with conservative overlap duration and return to the visible specimen without first discovering a hidden rule. This is temporal control, not a required exploration phase, in all five difficulties and both interaction modes.

source_evidence.claim: The renderer maps cage, specimen, and crate heights directly to bottom percentages on one vertical track; the specimen wake also consists of vertical positions.
Cage, specimen, crate, and wake are centered at the same horizontal coordinate with planar CSS artwork; containment styling changes borders or glow without introducing depth-dependent geometry.
The authoritative overlap conditions compare vertical center distance against the difference between cage and target half-heights.
The specimen evolves according to motion laws; cage velocity persists under thrust, gravity, drag, and boundary rebound; per-tick containment fills or drains progress and controls terminal outcomes.
Simulation ticks advance with elapsed task time and retain only the configured recent specimen positions for the visible wake.
Full mode binds Space keydown and keyup to engaged-state changes; simplified buttons latch the same engaged or disengaged state, preserving the need to switch ongoing acceleration at the right time.
Specimen absence drains capture reserve, crate progress persists after containment, zero reserve fails, and specimen completion passes only if crate progress is already complete.

Crate positions are separated from the specimen at spawn; generation accepts worlds where a private reference allocation policy succeeds while the reference specimen-only policy fails, with material exclusive crate service. This is supporting implementation evidence, not a general screenshot-only solver proof.

The canonical baseline is difficulty 4/full. All five parameter profiles retain inertial movement, positive specimen drain, accumulating crate service, and the same two-target success condition; interaction modes change the input surface.
Exported verification reloads the independent Ballast Lantern grader and replays exported result, truth, and public state, preserving the same completion dependency.

Active rendering updates positions, current containment styling, a motion beacon when enabled, wake dots, and winch state. It renders neither capture_meter nor crate_meter or a distinct crate-completion cue.

The full browser layout contains the shaft, winch controls, and terminal/readout controls, with no progress display or inspection control. The only optional panel is the developer cheat panel, outside a normal solution.
The shared readout helper only writes the caller's message; it does not add missing meter feedback. Developer cheat mode is separately gated by a URL parameter.
The shared mechanic dispatch supplies DOM/readout/cheat/action-clock helpers and delegates the complete task rendering to the mechanic; it does not supply progress widgets.

Termination produces generic PASS/FAIL; the browser does not display the grader's numerical reserve and crate feedback to support threshold learning. A failed response may replace the shaft with a fresh generated state.

The provided solver loads hidden ground truth, directly reads page simulation state including both meters, and uses private reserve thresholds to switch targets. Its successful operation cannot establish whether screenshot-only interaction must discover those thresholds.
Fill meters are internal; overlap and targets are visible and the two input surfaces are explicitly described.

limitations: Source-based classification; not an observed human or screenshot-only agent pass, and not an exhaustive proof over every conceivable solving policy.

baseline_description.interaction: Drag a brass handle around its disc far enough to request one clockwise or counter-clockwise sixth-turn.
baseline_description.difficulty: The baseline restores a rose sampled at exact shortest-path depth ten.

rationale.visual: The agent must distinguish piece shapes, colors, and motifs, match their positions to the reference, identify membership in overlapping circular groups, and interpret clockwise versus counter-clockwise movement in a plane. Both displays use the same fixed two-dimensional slot geometry; no depth or three-dimensional orientation is needed.
rationale.temporal: The complete current piece arrangement and target remain visible. Legality and move effects depend only on that current arrangement, so solving does not require a vanished earlier arrangement or interpreting continuous motion. A full-mode drag is accepted from the angular difference between its start and release coordinates; no duration, speed, intermediate path, or evolving world state is tested. It can be executed as a fixed spatial gesture. Learning from attempted turns supplies action-effect feedback, which alone does not establish a nontrivial temporal requirement. This also applies to simplified button input at difficulties 1 through 5.
rationale.reasoning_planning: A turn cyclically permutes six pieces, some shared with other discs. The heart must belong to the chosen disc and foreign pointed pieces must be absent from it. Moving those pieces therefore changes which later rotations are possible, and a locally attractive piece placement can interfere with subsequent restoration. The agent must infer these constraints and choose a dependent sequence of moves. All five profiles retain this problem, with exact scramble depths 2, 4, 7, 10, and 14; even the shallowest is a dependent two-turn restoration, not independent piece matching.
rationale.exploration_interface: The visible text states only the restoration goal. The page does not explain the heart/point legality rules, mark which discs are currently legal, or show refusal feedback; an illegal request leaves the visible rose unchanged. A screenshot-only agent must probe controls and use the resulting acceptance or lack of movement to learn their effects and restrictions. This is learning an undisclosed interaction rule, beyond receiving the next ordinary task state. Simplified mode makes direction and disc selection explicit through buttons but still does not disclose legality, so it retains this capability. No difficulty profile adds rule explanations or legality cues.

source_evidence.claim: The task has three overlapping planar six-slot discs, thirteen fixed 2D positions, and visually differentiated heart, pointed, and shield pieces with colors and motifs.
SVG renders each piece at its current slot and displays a reference rendered from solved_state alongside the current rose; there is no 3D transform or hidden face needed for matching.

Turns are discrete current-state permutations, the current and reference states remain visible, and the drag commits only on release using a signed endpoint angle threshold of 0.45 radians. Holding duration and intermediate movement do not affect success.

Grading replays legal state permutations and checks exact final restoration. The transcript has no action timestamp or duration requirement, and no hidden prior state affects the legal action beyond the current visible permutation.

Legal moves require the heart in the selected disc and no foreign point within it. Each move permutes six shared slots, changing later legality. The generator samples exact-depth states in this constrained state graph rather than imposing an unrelated move quota.
The independent verifier repeats the same state-dependent legality and rotation logic and requires exact restoration, confirming that later action consequences are part of the accepted task.

All disc rings use the same class with no legal-move indicator. Full mode has handles and no instruction block; simplified mode has labelled arrow buttons. The rendered page supplies the goal and reference but no legality explanation. Refused attempts do not update the visible rose or show a message, requiring probes to discover restrictions.

Every configured depth samples only states with at least one illegal disc, and the public prompt contains only the restoration goal. The control condition changes scramble depth without supplying rule instructions.

The canonical baseline is difficulty 4/full. All five difficulty profiles vary only scramble_depth (2, 4, 7, 10, 14); both interaction profiles request the same clockwise or counter-clockwise disc turns. These profiles do not introduce a different capability requirement.

The scripted solver reads ground_truth.json and follows its solution_moves while inspecting the private browser model. Its success cannot establish that screenshot-only agents receive the needed rules or solution path without probing.

baseline_description.interaction: Scroll the visible linked planes, orbit the visible mesh by dragging empty glass, drag mesh nodes to merge, and click slice nodes for seeds.
baseline_description.difficulty: Reconstruct four intertwined fibres with two missing continuations and two false joins; regenerated topology must be inspected between repairs.

rationale.visual: The decision concerns continuation and separation of fibres in a three-coordinate volume. The linked orthogonal slices expose different coordinate pairs and select nodes by the omitted coordinate; the orbitable reconstruction projects the same 3D positions. Nearby decoy nodes and crossing paths must be disambiguated by depth and continuity, rather than treating every projected overlap or existing connection as a true continuation. Node labels are opaque and colours outside the marked component do not encode fibre membership.
rationale.temporal: A solution can work from successive stable views of the current specimen. Geometry does not evolve independently; every node and current edge remains in the reconstruction, and the current anchor component, selected segments, seed labels, and slice indices remain visible. A chosen slice and camera angle persist until changed, permitting local inspection and repair without recalling a vanished task state or interpreting motion. Full-mode orbit depends on pointer displacement and merge depends on the drag endpoints, with no duration or moving-target requirement. The required edit-then-slice-change sequence is an interface gate followed by a static result, not by itself temporal understanding.
rationale.reasoning_planning: The agent must infer which gaps continue the marked fibre and which existing edges incorrectly connect a neighbour. Choosing a merge changes the connected component, while choosing a cut must remove the spurious connection without cutting a true continuation. The grader rejects any merge outside the constructed missing edges and any cut outside the constructed false joins, then requires the exact repaired topology and target component. This is a connectivity and continuity decision, not merely recognising a marked colour or copying a visible label.
rationale.exploration_interface: The agent actively changes slice depth and viewing angle to reveal the spatial evidence needed at ambiguous joins; all three current slices expose only a bounded part of the volume. In full mode it also has to discover the canvas interaction mapping: the visible form omits the labelled merge and orbit controls, while empty-space drags orbit, node-to-node drags merge, scrolling a slice changes its plane, and slice clicks place seeds. Simplified mode exposes these controls explicitly, but still requires active inspection of the volume. The mandatory post-edit inspection count alone is not the basis for this label.

source_evidence.claim: Nodes have three-coordinate positions; slices retain nodes within a normal-coordinate band. Public labels and identifiers are opaque, selected neighbouring nodes are placed near target nodes in all three coordinates, and missing and false edges alter the topology.

Linked views and the yaw/pitch projection use the same geometry. The mesh displays current edges and opaque node labels; highlighting follows the current anchor-connected component rather than hidden true fibre identity.

Current selections and seed labels are redrawn visibly. Slice and camera changes are driven by explicit input, with persistent focus and camera state. Orbit uses displacement from pointer-down and merges use endpoints; no duration, velocity, timed exposure, or autonomous geometry update enters these actions.

Replay checks action order, current geometry, camera displacement, visible seed locations, and an inspection after every edit. It does not check elapsed time or hold duration. The inspection requirement can be met by a slice change presenting the new static topology.

The generated public specimen contains its initial connectivity and a target anchor, while the target membership, true topology, missing joins, and false joins are retained in grading truth. Thus a visible solution must infer repairs from the specimen rather than read an answer list.

Only constructed missing joins may be merged and constructed false joins may be cut. Certification requires exact true edges and exactly the target anchor component, making the connectivity consequences of each repair relevant.

The visible planes reveal only slices of the volume and can be moved independently. Full mode hides the labelled orbit, plane-step, merge, and segment-palette controls; canvas gestures implement inspection, merge, and seed placement. Simplified mode exposes labelled controls over the same geometry.
The is-hidden class actually removes the simplified controls from display, and canvas cursors provide only generic crosshair/grab affordances in full mode.

The canonical baseline is difficulty 4/full. All five profiles retain multiple fibres, missing and false joins, linked slices, and the same task goal; their active parameters vary counts and crossing density. Both interaction profiles preserve topology and expose different input controls. No profile removes the repair inference or active viewing problem.

All five difficulty parameter sets feed the same geometry, missing/false-edge generation, slicing, and repair requirements. Interaction changes the selected surface rather than the generated decision problem. No supported capability exception was found among the ten difficulty/interaction combinations.

rationale.visual: The necessary spatial information is planar: distinguish the two labeled compartments, locate empty membrane slots and the eject/fuel drop surfaces, and compare concentration-bar endpoints with target intervals. No depth, three-dimensional orientation, occlusion inference, or perspective transformation is involved.
rationale.temporal: A general solution can rely on current counts, persistent crossing counters and recipe completion rather than interpreting motion or recalling vanished state. Leak removal need not be precisely timed because extra diffusion can be corrected with the explicit solute adjusters. Pumping can finish automatically when a finite ATP supply is exhausted, or the pumps can be ejected after their persistent completion indicators are satisfied. With transport stopped, the target condition is static and the six-tick stability check advances automatically to a visible READY TO LOCK state. There is no required held input during that check. Ordinary drags have fixed endpoints and no minimum-duration requirement. Thus the animated particles, crossing wait, and automatic stability wait do not establish a necessary temporal capability under the current guideline.
rationale.reasoning_planning: The baseline combines a passive leak obligation with two directed ATP pumps and final target intervals. The solver must reconcile the leak's concentration changes with later pump transfers, allocate fuel across the installed pumps, and choose whether further fuel or a signed compartment adjustment will reach the target without subsequent transport undoing it. An edit to a species changes the state against which its later transfers and final bands are evaluated. The visible recipe supplies transporter identities and broad order, but it does not supply the required fuel allocation or seed- and intervention-dependent concentration corrections.
rationale.exploration_interface: The UI already displays required transporter identities, each protein's species and direction, ATP dependence, target intervals, labeled interaction surfaces, and solute-adjuster effects. configuration_exceptions.reason: Difficulty 1 requires only the named sodium pump, no passive leak, three pump cycles and an ATP burst of exactly three units. source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 selects one species, zero required leaks, three pump cycles, wide targets and a three-unit ATP burst, with explicit place/fuel/wait instructions.

baseline_description.difficulty: The baseline restores twelve faces, including four rim slivers, after four coupled twists.

rationale.visual: The necessary spatial information consists of colored sectors, heptagon boundaries, neighboring faces, and their positions relative to a central turning aperture in a two-dimensional hyperbolic disc. Re-centering changes the planar projection and scale. There is no depth, hidden rear surface, or three-dimensional object relationship to reconstruct.
rationale.temporal: The puzzle has no motion-based clue, elapsed-time condition, disappearing clue, or continuously advancing state. Current sticker colors remain rendered, and compressed regions can be revisited by changing the view. The scramble is supplied as an already scrambled static arrangement, not a demonstration that must be remembered. Each twist immediately produces the next static arrangement. A full-mode drag can be a spatial move from a visible face toward the center; its success does not depend on speed or hold duration. Planning from the current board and learning the fixed input rules do not require reconstructing an earlier hidden puzzle state. This No label is provisional pending the separate temporal audit.
rationale.reasoning_planning: A turn shifts both the selected face's seven sectors and seven sectors distributed across nearby faces. The agent must infer the transfer constraints and choose face/direction combinations whose effects leave every face monochrome within the move budget. The baseline is generated at exact solution depth four with a budget of six; independent color matching or rotating each mixed face in isolation does not solve the coupled permutation problem.
rationale.exploration_interface: The visible baseline gives the goal, turn counter, dashed circle, RESET SCRAMBLE, and CERTIFY, but no drag/click gesture legend or explanation of the turning aperture and neighboring-sticker cycle. Interaction is needed to discover view movement, which clicks turn a face, and what those turns affect. Re-centering also makes compressed rim stickers inspectable. Simplified mode labels turn directions but still does not explain the face-click centering operation or sticker-transfer rule, so it retains this requirement. This is learning the available operations and their consequences, beyond routine progress feedback.

source_evidence.claim: The generated world consists of planar complex-coordinate heptagons and their two-coordinate centers and vertices; active faces are selected from a reflected planar tiling.
The same two-dimensional transformed geodesic paths draw colored sectors and identify clicked faces; the dashed central aperture is a visible circle in that plane.

Sticker updates are discrete synchronous twists; view changes are pointer-coordinate transforms or immediate focus clicks. Initialization draws a fixed initial state, and reset restores it. There is no timer, motion progression, minimum hold, or animation-dependent target in these task operations.

Replay uses ordered view and sticker transformations and a move budget, with no event time, drag duration, or elapsed-time condition. Current state suffices to determine each legal sticker update and final monochrome completion.

Each turn couples a seven-sector own-face cycle with a seven-position ring drawn from nearby faces; generated scrambles are rejected if a shorter-than-configured solution exists. The goal requires all faces to be monochrome.

The exported verifier independently replays the actual permutations, enforces the central aperture and finite twist budget, and accepts only a monochrome resulting state. Merely claiming completion or selecting a matching color cannot pass.

Full mode's control markup is empty; the visible page states the goal without its input rules. Actual handlers implement drag-to-pan, left/right click-to-twist inside the aperture, and simplified click-to-center. Twist coupling is implemented but not explained by visible text.

RESET SCRAMBLE restores both original sticker state and move allowance, supporting repeatable visible probing of the unexplained operations. Simplified turn buttons require a focused face and otherwise display NO FACE CENTERED.
The scripted solver reads ground_truth.json and solution_moves before executing UI actions; its success does not establish that the screenshot-only user is given a solution sequence.

Both interaction surfaces operate on the same puzzle. None changes dimensionality or introduces timed progression. D1 still requires identifying the inverse face/direction permutation; simplified mode still leaves centering and sticker-transfer behavior to discover. No supported category-level exception was found across the ten profiles.

limitations: No screenshot-only gameplay or rendering check was performed. rationale.visual: The necessary spatial information is planar grid occupancy, cardinal adjacency, wall connectivity, and the relative positions of the player, sentries, strike tiles, and stair. Movement and attacks use two-coordinate cells and Manhattan adjacency. The board's slight rotation and shaded tokens do not require depth or 3D geometry. This remains true for the 7-, 8-, and 9-cell board profiles and both interaction modes.
rationale.temporal: Successful actions are gated to the first 1150 ms of each recurring 1800 ms beat, with only one accepted action per beat. Sentries advance at beat boundaries even when the player does nothing; enemy shield and strike phases determine whether an attack or adjacent position is safe. The screenshot-only player must coordinate input execution with the gold window and the evolving combat state. Current enemy phases and their successors are displayed, so hidden phase memory is unnecessary; the positive label rests on timing and temporal control. Every difficulty retains the same beat gate, including difficulty 1 with only a crawler, and both keyboards and buttons are subject to it. This is a provisional temporal finding.
rationale.reasoning_planning: At the baseline, moving changes where pursuers will move or attack at the next boundary, while attacking leaves the player in place and can expose it to retaliation. The agent must choose attack, movement, and wait actions that defeat the two-hit crawler, alternating armored hopper, and rooted striker before its three hearts run out, then reach the stair. Walls, enemy blocking, and numbered movement order affect later positions. These are consequences to anticipate beyond recognizing a target. Difficulties 1-3 reduce enemy kinds and health but still require choosing a route and combat position against moving pursuers; difficulty 5 adds another striker and fewer hearts. Neither input mode removes the action dependencies.
rationale.exploration_interface: The initial draw exposes the full board and all enemy positions, health dots, current phases, successor phases, and behavior descriptions before the clock starts. The interface explicitly explains movement-to-attack, numbered enemy order, directional tie-breaking, blocked paths, beat gating, and the exit condition. The clock-start control begins the encounter rather than revealing a concealed rule or location. Later board and roster updates and attack feedback are routine visible combat state, so no necessary exploratory probing or interface discovery is established. All five difficulty profiles use these same disclosures in both interaction modes.

source_evidence.claim: The board is rendered cell by cell from two-coordinate positions; directional moves, adjacent attacks, walls, enemies, stair, player, and strike danger all occupy the same planar grid.

Connecting hubs fixes distances that constrain the machine's later motion; a legal arrangement can still fail delivery. All profiles retain this dependency. There is no concealed course region, hidden per-instance material or motor mapping, or prerequisite probe needed to obtain the construction problem. Run feedback can support optional design iteration, but it is the physical outcome of an already chosen construction, not a mandatory discovery step. At difficulties 4 and 5, the persistent thumb and indicator geometry still provides current values, so the reduced numeric readouts do not force memory.
rationale.reasoning_planning: Baseline calibration has a concrete action dependency beyond independently matching values. An upstream correction changes a downstream control, but only a direct source-change event ending at its target releases that source's outgoing lock. A coupled source can therefore already be correct while its next channel stays locked; the agent must choose an initially off-target move and a return move to produce the required release, then complete the affected downstream settings. For example, the generated baseline seed capability-audit-12 starts CABIN ENVELOPE at 45/80 with target 20/55. Moving LOW to 20 also moves HIGH to 55, yet HIGH must subsequently move away and back to release HYDRAULIC BAND LOW. This evidence supports the label without treating every target match or printed sequence as planning.
rationale.exploration_interface: Opening every named circuit branch and matching each displayed current state to the persistent target card is routine required navigation. Every circuit is required, headings expose disclosure controls and circuit counts, and the UI explicitly instructs the player to disclose parent bays and set state cells. The prescribed low-then-high progression does not itself establish planning.

A general reactive solution exchanges a left-heavy pair, otherwise advances, and seals after correcting the last available comparison. Generator rejection guarantees completion by this visible stopping condition. It requires neither past readings nor motion interpretation, elapsed duration, or a timed release. Learned-relation and insertion witnesses determine reading allowances below the specified memoryless cyclic witness, while identities and decorative features are not exact weight labels.
The metered visible-label solver carries pivot, ordered prefix, search interval and comparison outcomes forward across carriage moves.

configuration_exceptions.reason: The selected adjacent pair starts NOT WEIGHED and travel does not reveal its relation. A limited WEIGH action reveals the heavier specimen. The agent must choose which previously unknown comparisons to obtain and use those observations to arrange further comparisons and finish the order. This is active information gathering through the comparator; the control meanings themselves are explicit. source_evidence.claim: Manual mode adds WEIGH, initially suppresses the verdict, clears it after advancement, and reveals the result only after a metered measurement.
All metered profiles use hidden exact weights within one displayed size band and limit readings below the specified reactive measurement policy; D4/D5 further constrain direct-pair caching.
A visible solution deliberately brings chosen pivot/anchor specimens adjacent, weighs them, and uses the new verdict to choose the next comparison or insertion position.
The UI presents a planar row, highlighted adjacent windows, specimen identities and slot numbers, and an explicit heavier-side lamp and text verdict. Specimen canvases are two-dimensional drawings.

The baseline lever allowance covers all available advances plus the maximum inversion-removing exchanges and slack. Continuing the reactive policy until the visible reading counter reaches zero therefore supplies a stopping rule without remembering previous comparisons.

Automatic readings remain measured and update on each action; advance changes the static cursor and increments the reading counter. No animation or clock drives the puzzle state. Full-mode actions commit on a release inside a fixed lower detent, with no timing or duration checks.

The whole-row goal is ascending weight. EXCHANGE permutes the current two identities, ADVANCE selects an overlapping adjacent pair cyclically, and SEAL checks the whole row. A local exchange changes the objects and constraints faced later.

Independent replay binds each event to the actual current pair, applies swaps and carriage advancement, enforces reserves, and accepts only a sealed globally ascending order. Successful recognition without the appropriate sequence of state-changing ordering actions cannot pass.
The canonical instructions explicitly name ADVANCE, EXCHANGE and SEAL and explain that the lamp reports the heavier side of its current pair.

In the automatic baseline the initial and subsequent current-pair verdicts are supplied automatically; no WEIGH action exists. The explicit measurement action and unmeasured state occur only in manual profiles.

The visible-label solver uses optional remembered relations for early completion but also implements the zero-remaining-reading stopping condition. Its use of memory is therefore not evidence that the automatic baseline requires memory.
The exported verifier loads result, truth and public state and invokes the same independent comparator replay grader; it does not accept an asserted success without the ordering transcript.

baseline_description.interaction: Select instrument, drag from first anchor to second.
baseline_description.difficulty: Find the circumcenter by coupling perpendicular bisectors of two sides.

rationale.visual: The task requires locating planar triangle vertices, circle-circle crossings, and line-line crossings and relating them to the visible target. All implemented geometry is Euclidean geometry in two screen coordinates; there is no depth or viewpoint inference.
rationale.temporal: The givens, target, constructed objects, and crossings remain visible. Construction actions operate on fixed endpoints: full mode records the pointer-down and pointer-up anchors, with no required duration, motion interpretation, or path-dependent effect. A solution can leave the givens unchanged and build from successive static views. Optional dragging of givens is unnecessary, and the grader's automatic perturbation replay requires no temporal observation from the player. This remains a provisional temporal judgment.
rationale.reasoning_planning: The gold marker exposes the desired location but does not provide a legal free-placement point. The agent must choose circles and lines whose derived intersections establish the required invariant: equal-radius circles provide a perpendicular bisector, and two such bisectors supply the circumcenter. Earlier constructions enable later anchors, and the grader replays their dependencies on eight other triangles, so visual approximation alone cannot solve the task. All five difficulty profiles retain a construction dependency: D1 joins the supplied circles' crossings before marking the segment midpoint; D2 constructs the circles and bisector; D3 combines two bisectors; D4 constructs altitudes; D5 constructs internal angle bisectors and a perpendicular radius for the incircle. Both interaction modes preserve these requirements.
rationale.exploration_interface: The initial UI states the goal, legal anchors, tool effects, gesture, stroke budget, and perturbation test. New crossings appear automatically as the deterministic result of a chosen construction and persist afterward. This is task progression rather than a requirement to uncover hidden information or discover an unknown control mapping. Reshaping a given is available as an optional check, but a known geometric construction solves every profile without using it. Simplified mode explicitly instructs two anchor clicks; full mode explicitly instructs dragging between them.

source_evidence.claim: All construction and target calculations use two-component points, planar line/circle intersections, and Euclidean triangle centers.
The canvas displays the construction objects, dashed target, given points, derived crossings, and marked point; picking uses proximity to these actual planar anchors.

All derived points are rendered; gesture instructions are mode-specific, and ordinary construction actions immediately expose their crossings. Optional given-point manipulation is not a prerequisite for constructing or submitting.

baseline_description.interaction: Full interaction; see the task instructions for its input controls.
baseline_description.difficulty: Variable island and delivery direction, a low landing shelf, and a 100–120 unit receiving well.

rationale.visual: The parcel is an axis-aligned rectangle in a side-on plane. Successful movement depends on its width and height relative to visible floor support, gap width, shelf clearance, the well opening, and circular seals. Fixed area couples width and height, but neither the rendering nor collision geometry requires depth or a 3D transformation. All five difficulty profiles and both input modes use this same 2D representation.
rationale.temporal: The baseline requires sustaining and releasing body-arrow inputs while acceleration, residual horizontal velocity, morphing, and gravity continue. Reaching the offset island seal and stopping under the well require controlling when movement ends or reverses; letting every movement continue to a boundary is unsafe on the island. This is time-extended action control under the temporal guideline, even without a memory task. Simplified interaction normally retains evolving movement because its buttons latch a direction until another command. Difficulty 2 still requires changing shape or stopping before a tall parcel crosses the floor gap, and difficulties 3-5 retain the island and well problem. Difficulty 1 Full still requires a sustained pointer hold. Difficulty 1 Simplified has an endpoint-only route and is recorded as an exception.
rationale.reasoning_planning: The agent must choose a feasible support route, collect the island's overhead seal before leaving, and arrange changes of shape so the parcel is wide enough to span the gap and low enough to fit under shelves before becoming narrow and tall in the receiving well. The consequences matter later: an unsupported narrow crossing loses the parcel, and extending beneath a solid shelf cannot reach the well seal. Difficulty 4 and 5 tighten the same dependencies. Difficulty 2 substitutes a linear tunnel/gap route but still requires coordinating reach, clearance, and support. Difficulty 1 removes the gap, yet a solution must choose a height fitting both clearance and reach, or traverse low first and grow for a return pass; it retains an action dependency rather than requiring only seal recognition.
rationale.exploration_interface: The canvas displays all solids and all seal locations from the start, and collected seals remain visibly marked. The controls and instructions explicitly communicate sliding, taller/wider morphing, fixed area, no jumping, and release or COAST. No information panel, hidden obstacle, randomized control mapping, or probing action must be discovered. Watching movement and collection feedback while executing the visible geometry-based plan is routine control feedback, not a required information-revealing exploration phase. This remains true across all difficulty and interaction profiles.

configuration_exceptions.reason: A general route can click RIGHT at the initial height of 80 and let the parcel stop at the right room boundary, collecting the two low seals en route. It can then click TALLER and let height reach its cap of 200, followed by LEFT, which collects both elevated seals before reaching the tunnel. Difficulty 1 has continuous floor and clearance 105, so the first traverse fits and the tall return cannot fall into a gap. All intermediate decisions can be made at static endpoints; no hold, precisely timed release, velocity estimate, or remembered transient is required. A 100-seed Python physics replay of these three latched commands passed all cases; that check is implementation evidence, not browser gameplay verification.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 has clearance 105, no floor gap, reach 100, and no alcove.

The continuous floor, initial height 80, maximum height 200, and seal positions support an initial low rightward traverse followed by a tall leftward return across the configuration's randomized room positions.

Morphing saturates at the height cap, movement stops at solid or room boundaries, and Simplified commands remain latched after a click. These natural endpoints remove the need for duration-sensitive switching on the described route.
Parcel bounds are area/height in an axis-aligned 2D rectangle; the canvas draws the actual rectangular solids, circular seals, and parcel in that plane.
Collision and seal collection use the same planar rectangle and circle geometry, so the relevant spatial task is 2D.

The grader replays controls for their actual tick durations, including inertia, gravity, falls, and morphing, and enforces the selected hold or latch input surface.
The exported verifier independently invokes the physical transcript grader; a claimed completion without the corresponding timed physics does not pass.

The lower profiles construct a tunnel and optional gap. The baseline and higher profiles generate a reflected island with two different support choices, a low landing shelf, and a high seal in a receiving well; these create concrete route and shape dependencies.

Morphs and translations that overlap solids are blocked, unsupported parcels fall, and all seals must be physically contacted. Choosing the correct sequence of shapes therefore affects later reachability.

The initial rendering exposes the complete world and seal positions, explicit mode-specific control instructions, and a persistent collection count. Input events operate those named controls without revealing a hidden map or behavior mapping.
The task instructions disclose fixed area, no jumping, falling without support, and how to engage and release each interaction mode.

rationale.reasoning_planning: The agent must design surfaces whose slope, endpoints and position redirect gravity-driven particles into the proper gates, then account for the effect of permanent earlier ink on future routing. At baseline, a later route must intercept the stream upstream while the previous route has already supplied its jar, and the final route must contact the plate to obtain the third colour. Grains and batches advance automatically; hopper colour, jar tallies and required counts, current batch, waste, ink and stock are visible. A completed jar's count persists, permitting a current-screen threshold policy instead of estimating motion or timing a colour transition.

Replay simulates automatic falling and permanent lines, accepting success when every jar has its required pure fill. It imposes no requirement to use the canonical batch-switch times; event ticks only determine when supplied geometry enters the physical world.
Seeded reflected and shifted geometry places separated jars, a sloped recolouring plate over the last jar, and level-dependent pegs; the world limits ink and requires a pure fill in every jar.

Line slope and contact change particle motion, the plate changes colour, wrong-colour gates block passage, and permanent line length consumes ink. Success depends on the downstream physical consequences of constructed routes.

baseline_description.interaction: Click the moving gateway cards directly, use the ledger tabs, and drag each physical switch handle between NO and YES; stationary clicks do not change switches.

rationale.visual: The necessary spatial information is planar: associate each written statement with its adjacent rail, distinguish the handle's left NO and right YES positions, locate drawer tabs, and target the visible centers of orbiting cards. The orbit is a 2D ellipse; shadows, slight rotations, and changing overlap do not require depth reconstruction or 3D reasoning.
rationale.temporal: At D3/full the entry and final options change screen coordinates continuously. A successful direct click must land inside the moving card, and the grader checks its pointer geometry against its phase at task time. Thus execution must account for the evolving target position. This demand concerns the action as well as observation. The static switch drags have no duration threshold and do not independently establish a temporal requirement. rationale.reasoning_planning: The goal is to block every optional purpose, but an affirmative permission requires NO while a negatively worded refusal requires YES. The agent must infer the answer from each statement's polarity, reject gateway wording that accepts additional purposes, avoid resetting completed choices, and choose a final action that preserves those choices. The grader requires all six answers to match their semantic targets and a commit decision. The baseline has no cross-switch dependency; those dependencies appear at D4 and D5.
rationale.exploration_interface: The visible gateway labels, NO/YES endpoints, named drawer tabs, review action, and return action supply a direct solution. Opening the ledger and switching its labeled drawers simply displays the next set of required statements. Current answers remain available whenever a drawer is reopened. Neither hidden clues nor experimental use of the reset control is required, and ordinary use of the visible switch affordance does not establish exploration. D4/D5 expose directed links on the affected rows and can also be solved without probing: first visit the drawers to correct outgoing source switches, then revisit the drawers to reconcile the other visible answers. source_evidence.claim: D1/D2 set moving_gateways false, orbit speed zero, drawer_count one and link_count zero.
A switch drag succeeds from fixed start/end geometry and movement samples; no duration or continuing effect is measured.
Switch gesture replay checks endpoints, travel and sample count, without a duration requirement.

configuration_exceptions.reason: Every gateway label is duplicated on a stationary proxy and every answer can be set using fixed NO/YES buttons. At D4/D5, linked sources can be corrected during a pass through the drawers, followed by a pass correcting the other current visible answers. Links are disjoint directed pairs, sources start incorrect, and visible notes identify source and target roles; this solution does not require recalling a disappeared answer, interpreting motion, or sustaining an action. Labeled drawer traversal and reinspection do not independently constitute a nontrivial temporal relationship.

source_evidence.claim: Simplified mode provides fixed labeled gateway proxies and SET NO/SET YES buttons; directed links are printed on affected rows.
Changing drawers preserves all purpose answers and only changes which drawer is displayed.
Each directed link uses a disjoint pair of purpose IDs and each source starts opposite its target answer, allowing sources to be fixed before target reconciliation.
Simplified gateway input uses option_proxy and is not subjected to the full moving-card pointer-geometry check.

configuration_exceptions.reason: D1 has only one action at each gateway, three affirmative permission statements whose requested answer is uniformly NO, and no reset or linked controls. The agent can directly apply the stated refusal goal to each independent visible switch and use the sole final action. It need not resolve inverted statements, discriminate competing consent outcomes, or choose an order that affects later answers.

source_evidence.claim: D1 has negative_count zero, entry_option_count and final_option_count one, and no reset traps or links.
A gateway with one option contains only its correct action.
With negative_count zero every generated purpose has the same False target.
With an empty link list each switch affects only its own answer.
Gateway centers follow a planar cosine/sine ellipse and the visible cards contain the decision labels.
Each statement is placed beside a rail with visible NO and YES endpoints and a current answer state.
The handle's horizontal position encodes its Boolean answer; purpose controls use a flat row layout.
The canonical baseline is difficulty 3/full, with moving gateways at 14 degrees per second; difficulties 1 and 2 disable gateway motion.
Full input records click coordinates and card geometry while requestAnimationFrame updates card positions from elapsed task time.

Full gateway gestures are checked against the orbital phase and card bounds at event time, so merely selecting a button through a keyboard-generated click with absent pointer geometry is not a stationary-input solution.
Visible copy distinguishes affirmative permission statements, negative blocking statements, privacy-management gateways, and accept/reset decoys.
Affirmative statements have False targets while negative statements have True targets; initial answers are randomized.
Choosing an accept option at either gateway terminates with an acceptance decision rather than the required commit.
Passing requires a committed decision, every purpose matching its semantic target, and activation of any configured directed links.
Purpose wording, endpoint labels, directed-link notes, drawer labels, and provider-reset labels are rendered directly; drawer changes reveal another explicitly labeled page of statements.
Answers remain in the model when switching drawers; opening a drawer changes only the current drawer and redraws the persistent answers.
Visible tabs or previous/next controls select drawers, while a visible back button permits reinspection from the final stage. No probe is required to unlock a statement or infer a hidden goal.
The exported verifier loads the submitted result and reruns the independent consent grader; displayed completion alone does not determine success.
